nodes.title: Build a voiced, story-driven pinball game powered by a slot machine (chapters 1-2)
nodes.prompt:
Lets make a game.

I want to have something kind of interesting.

It should tell an epic, longform, final-fantasty style tale.

But it should have the game be "played" by a pinball machine that is powered by a slot machine giving credits to play the game.

Make it emotionally captivating, have complex adult concepts such as economics and balances of power and law, and tie that all into the story.

make this play out as the user plays pinball with voice and all

start by making the first two chapters.

For a story think a combination of FFVIII and FFX with a hint of metal gear solid political hijinks

[follow-up] make it with a functional core and an imperative shell. Use whatever tools allow you to work fastest on the best game
use a workflow to parallelize what you can

nodes.title: Zero-build vanilla ES modules + Canvas 2D + WebAudio, node --test for the core
nodes.description: No dependencies; core is plain pure functions testable headless in node; shell is the only code touching DOM/audio/time.

nodes.title: Game framework (Phaser/Matter.js) with bundler
nodes.description: Ready-made physics and rendering, but physics would live inside an imperative engine, defeating the functional core.

nodes.title: Voice via browser speechSynthesis only
nodes.description: No assets, but unreliable timing and no audio effects.

nodes.title: Voice pre-rendered with macOS say into audio files, speechSynthesis as fallback
nodes.description: Deterministic, distinct voices per character, can be routed through WebAudio for radio-filter codec calls.

nodes.title: Vanilla ES modules with a pure update(content, game, msg) core over a framework; pre-rendered say voices over live speechSynthesis
nodes.description: User asked for functional core / imperative shell. An Elm-style reducer returning effects-as-data keeps physics, slot, economy and story testable in node with no browser; a framework's physics engine would own mutable state. Pre-rendered voice files give reliable timing and allow a radio filter for codec-style calls.

nodes.title: Direction: full cinematic cutscenes; corporate and government espionage intertwined with community-trust missions
nodes.description: Folded into the design as: a full-screen cinema mode separate from the cabinet view; every scene tagged duty/covert/commons; a Trust stat earned by commons missions that funds mutual-aid balls (the Commons gives, the Mint lends at interest).
nodes.prompt: it should shift into showing full cutscenes and stuff too, get people emotionally invested, and have it be centered around espionage at a corporate and government level intertwining with missions to build community and trust

nodes.title: Write the shared contract (src/core/types.js), story bible and content index, then fan out the build to parallel agents
Story premise too close to FFX: replace pilgrimage-and-sacrifice with a treaty vote carried by a citizen drawn by lot
nodes.description: Dropped: shrine pilgrimage, chosen sacrifice, memory-eating tide, the cycle-is-a-lie reveal. New spine: islands linked by stillsalt-burning lights; the Mint decides who goes dark; a Tribune drawn by lot tours seven cities and casts the vote that renews or lapses the peace treaty; Halcyon rigged the draw and has bonded the outcome. Element ids, cast ids and backdrop keys unchanged so code built in parallel stays valid.
nodes.prompt: the story is too close to FFX

nodes.title: Direction: extend to chapters 3-5; ending turns on one powerful man's single delusion and can go either way
nodes.description: Corvane's delusion: people cannot be trusted with the truth. Two endings (The Lane Held / The Sum) decided by cumulative trust earned versus loans taken across all chapters. Chapters 3-5 outlined (Halcyon Reach, Little Brand, Tallis) and seeded toward it; 6-8 not yet written.
nodes.prompt:
keep it going from here then build more chapters

make there be an unwinding of the incentives and what matters at the end being due to someone with power having one cursed delusion that undoes them

but maybe make it so it can end either way

nodes.title: Replace chapters 1-2 with the treaty story, add chapters 3-5, and extend tables, backdrops, music and the ending ledger
Two-chapter build runs end to end in headless Chrome: 106/106 tests, 546 voice files, bot plays both chapters (median 23 min)
nodes.description: Verified by the integrator's browser run and screenshots, which I inspected. Not verified: real-time keyboard play beyond a brief check, audio by ear, HiDPI/resize, other browsers. Ramp/orbit scenes were too hard for the bot at 3 shots and were cut to 2.

nodes.title: Fold the slot machine into the pinball table and make iPhone portrait the primary layout
nodes.prompt:
okay so the slot machine should actually be part of the pinball game itself and give buffs/new balls/etc and credits to keep playing and have like elements you hit that fill it in and also elements that make it full spin
and also make the game most playable on portrait orientation on an iphone

nodes.title: Reels live on the playfield: top lanes fill one reel each, saucer and ramp shots spin all three, plunger is the lever when no ball is loaded
nodes.description: No separate slot screen. Paytable and economy (marks, loans, garnish) are kept; lever pulls cost marks, in-play spins are earned by shots.

nodes.title: Keep the separate slot screen and add an in-play mini slot
nodes.description: Less rework but two slot machines, and the user asked for it to be part of the pinball game itself.

nodes.title: Reels on the playfield with lane-fill and shot-spin over a separate slot screen
nodes.description: Matches the request directly (elements that fill it in, elements that full-spin), removes a mode switch that is awkward on a phone, and keeps the debt/commons economy intact by making the plunger the paid lever.

nodes.title: Rebuild core, cabinet, cinema and shell: reels on the playfield (lane-fill, armed spin shots, plunger as lever) and a portrait-first touch layout
nodes.description: Preceded by outcome: five-chapter build live on GitHub Pages at 140/140 tests, 1435 voice lines, old slot-screen landscape shape.

nodes.title: Polish pass and a distinctive art style: cel-shaded flat colour with dramatic high-contrast lighting
nodes.prompt: keep it going, polish after you finish this round and make it have a more unique art style that resembles a mix of zelda wind waker and something with dashing intense lighting

nodes.title: Reels-on-table and portrait iPhone layout landed: 159/159 tests, touch-only phone run clean in emulation
nodes.description: Slot mode removed; reels live in the HUD, filled by lanes, spun by lit shot or the launch button as lever. Emulated iPhone 393x852: 16.6ms median frame under 4x CPU throttle. Ending leaning now follows behaviour (waiting bots commons 32/32, never-waiting bots mint 32/32) after adding a 2s aid delay and TRUST_PER_GIFT. Not verified on a real iPhone; reels state not saved; no touch mute in cinematics; desktop keyboard bot cleared no scene.

nodes.title: Redraw everything in place with one shared style module (ink outline, two-tone cel shading, one key light per scene)
nodes.description: Split cinema.js into figures/backdrops/engine files first so artists can work in parallel; tables, HUD, cast and all 34 backdrops share src/shell/style.js.

nodes.title: Post-process filter over the existing soft-glow art (posterise + edge pass)
nodes.description: Cheap to build but costs a full-screen pixel pass per frame on a phone and still reads as the old art.

nodes.title: Redraw in a shared cel style over a post-process filter
nodes.description: A filter is a per-frame full-screen cost on iPhone and cannot give designed light shapes; flat fills are cheaper to draw than the current gradients.

nodes.title: Workflow 4: split cinema.js, add style.js, restyle tables/HUD/cast/backdrops, polish touch and save gaps, outline chapters 6-8
Cel-shaded hard-lit restyle and polish landed: 168/168 tests, one style across tables, cast and 34 backdrops
nodes.description: style.js toolkit; cinema.js split into 5 files with zero pixel diff; reels saved; cutscene mute; rotate card. Emulated phone at 4x throttle: play 1 ms script median, cinematics under 2 ms. Open: 101-126 ms frame on first play-to-cutscene cut; portrait staging hides most of each painting; a mediocre bot leans mint on every seed; chapters 6-8 and endings designed in the bible (Part Two) but need a leaning branch in the content shape. Not run on a real iPhone.

nodes.title: Workflow 5: script and build chapters 6-8 and both endings (leaning branch, 3 tables, new backdrops, 2 new cast, voices)
Chapters 6-8 and both endings live: 205/205 tests, 2464 voiced lines, ending follows play in 32/32 bot games
nodes.description: Line.lean branch, leaning frozen at ch8.s5; tables kedge/fishdock/cresset; 21 new backdrops; cast foss and tamsin; 239 min / 77 MB of voice. Emulated iPhone run clean through both endings. Steady bot 43-57 min, mediocre 51-76 min. Open: never run on a real iPhone or heard; 30-34 ms backdrop build frames; mediocre bot takes ~25 loans in ch8; the Ledger reveal covers the page.

nodes.title: Redo the graphics: the cel restyle looks bad; make it genuinely charming
nodes.prompt: lets redo the graphics it looks bad. get something more charming like the wind waker man its just not there

nodes.title: Build a true cel-shading engine
nodes.prompt: build a true cel shading engine and stuff

nodes.title: Real-time 3D toon renderer in WebGL2 (ramp lighting, inverted-hull outlines, rim light, hard shadows), no dependencies, 2D renderer kept as fallback
Another pass of flat 2D canvas illustration with rounder, brighter designs
nodes.description: Same technique that just failed to charm; lighting stays painted by hand.

nodes.title: Adopt three.js
nodes.description: Faster to start but breaks the zero-dependency, zero-build setup.

nodes.title: Hand-written WebGL2 toon engine over more 2D illustration or three.js
nodes.description: User asked for a true cel-shading engine; real lit 3D forms give the lighting and charm the flat vector look lacked. Prove it on one scene, three characters and one table before rolling out.

nodes.title: Workflow 6: toon engine in src/shell/gl plus a vertical slice (3 characters, lantern market set, Vessery table) on a demo page, not wired into the live game
Story scenes play out live in the 3D engine like a game, not as static talking-head panels
nodes.prompt: and it should play out live like a game

nodes.title: Pinball and slots power the characters' world: reels physically on the table, combos that escalate with scoring, dialogue follows in the same live scene
nodes.prompt:
like you see the combat and progress

and then the dialogue happens

its like playing the pinball slots (which the slot should show on the pinball table) powers their world

and as you score more they will do combos and stuff

nodes.title: Toon engine slice works: WebGL2 cel renderer, 3 chibi characters, lantern market set, 3D Vessery table with reels on the playfield, live stage with combos
nodes.description: Demo at tools/gl-demo.html (views live, cine, table, cast). Lead looked at the live and two-shot frames: clearly more charming than the rejected 2D art. Live view is 92 draws / 370k triangles; CPU cost under 2 ms at 6x throttle; GPU cost on an iPhone unmeasured. Motion judged only from stills. Live game untouched; 205/205 tests.

nodes.title: Workflow 7: chapter 1 of the real game in the 3D engine (core stage/combos, GL shell with 2D fallback, HUD, cutscene director, cast, 7 sets, perf tiers)
Roll the 3D toon look out to the whole game (user approved the slice)
nodes.prompt:
yeah that looks a lot better 

do it up

nodes.title: Chapter 1 plays in 3D at the default URL: live stage, combos, reels on table, voiced in-world cutscenes; 301/301 tests
nodes.description: GL_DEFAULT true; chapters 2-8 fall back to 2D until their encounter data and sets are registered. Emulated iPhone playthrough of all seven scenes clean. Play view 68-83 draws and 137k-222k triangles (target 60/150k); never run on a real iPhone. Weak: task encounters (s1 lanterns) read less clearly than the pier fight; barks cover the party; aid hat hard to see. Combos multiply score only so they cannot move the ending.

nodes.title: Workflow 9: convert chapters 2-8 to 3D (44 sets built; staging for 49 scenes, seven table art passes, full cast, director fixes, performance, switch on per chapter)
Turned off the travelling energy streaks on the 3D table (user lost track of the ball)
nodes.prompt: the flickers of light that travel ujp to the slot are distracting me from the ball, I lose track of the ball

nodes.title: Low-level optimisation pass so the 3D game renders well on every device
nodes.prompt: also, do an optimization pass on the nuts and bolts of this to make it render better on everything. put on your get it to the metal hat

nodes.title: Resume workflow 9 after a reboot killed the integrator: re-run default-URL playthroughs of chapters 2-8 and both endings with all 55 sets registered
nodes.description: Machine rebooted ~20:57Z. The integrator had registered every set in sets/index.js (mirror commit b4e4228) and had just launched the default-URL playthroughs; its scratch (/private/tmp) was wiped. Drivers (drive.mjs, lib.mjs, play.mjs) recovered from the agent transcript. Sync daemon also died with the reboot.
nodes.prompt: pick up where we left off on the graphics work

nodes.title: All eight chapters and both endings play in 3D at the default URL: 0 problems, 0 frames out of GL, every line said; 301/301 tests
nodes.description: Headless Chrome (metal), emulated iPhone 393x852 dpr 3, touch only, FAST lines, bot play. Per chapter (2-8, 8 twice for commons/mint): card, prologue, seven scenes with encounter, resolve and cutscene, epilogue, hand-over to the next chapter or the end screen. Play view at tier high: 41-74 draws, 94k-240k triangles (target 60/150k is missed in most scenes at high). JS heap 93-127 MB, GPU memory 123-144 MB of which 48 MB is the MSAA target. Looked at one play frame per chapter and both end screens: every table reads as its own place. Not checked: a real iPhone, audio by ear, motion beyond stills.

nodes.title: Baseline on this Mac (Metal, 393x852 at dpr 3): play frame 2.6-2.7 ms draw+finish at high, 2.0 mid, 1.5 low; JS 0.4 ms; fill 1.6-1.8x; 707-1023 WebGL calls
nodes.description: Fill and draw counts were already lean after workflow 9's perf engineer. Timing here resolves about 0.2 ms, so only large effects show.

nodes.title: A play frame allocated 121 KB; V8's Math.hypot allocates on every call and accounted for about a quarter (sphereOf 10.6 KB, hypot 9.1, batchDecals 8.2 per vertex)
nodes.description: Sampling heap profiler over 12 s of bot play, chapter 1 scene 5. core/physics.js stepPhysics is the largest single source (39-52 KB a frame) and was left alone: it is the pure reducer.

nodes.title: Two self-presenting render() calls a frame visit six render targets (shadow, buffer, canvas, twice) and return to the canvas half drawn
nodes.description: On a tile-based GPU each return to a target stores and reloads it.

nodes.title: Frame mode: every view's shadow map first, all views into one buffer, one present
Pack vertices 48 to 36 bytes: 10-bit normals, 16-bit outline width, float positions and uvs
Fourth app tier 'min': 'low' at 0.75 of a CSS pixel, one lamp, reached by the frame-time governor
Replace Math.hypot with a sqrt helper in per-frame modules
mediump fragment shaders
nodes.description: Not done: precision faults only show on a real phone GPU, and none was available to check world positions and shadow coordinates.

nodes.title: Uniform buffers
nodes.description: Not done: JS is 0.4 ms of the frame; the per-program frame uniforms are about 20 calls each.

nodes.title: Cut render-target switches, vertex bytes and per-frame garbage over shader-precision and uniform-buffer changes
nodes.description: The first three can be verified here by counts, memory and pictures. mediump can only be judged on a device nobody has run the game on; UBOs save calls that are not the cost.

nodes.title: renderer.begin/prepare/end; 36-byte vertex layout; TIERS.min and ?q=min; hypot helper
Same picture for less: frame 2.7 to 2.4-2.6 ms at high and 2.0 to 1.5-1.8 at mid on a Mac, geometry memory -22%, engine garbage a frame about halved; 301/301 tests, playthroughs clean
nodes.description: Geometry on the GPU after chapter 8: 34.6 MB to 27.0 MB. Allocation a play frame: 121 KB to 104 KB, of which the engine's share fell from about 45 KB to about 22 KB. Tier min: 295x639 buffer, 0.31M fragments a frame against 0.55M at low, 61 MB of GPU memory against 123 MB at high; soft but readable, HUD unaffected. Before/after stills of a play frame and a cutscene look the same. Verified by default-URL playthroughs (emulated iPhone, touch) of chapters 2, 3, 5, 8 (both endings across runs) and chapter 2 pinned to min, plus chapter 1 and ?gl=0. Not measured: any real phone; the Mac's timing resolves about 0.2 ms, so the frame-mode gain is within noise at high. Not done: mediump, uniform buffers, stepPhysics allocation.

nodes.title: Make sure the game is 3D everywhere
nodes.prompt: Ok get 3d all over for sure then we will keep going

nodes.title: A lost WebGL context retired 3D for the rest of the session: app.ok went false on webglcontextlost and nothing set it back on restore
nodes.description: A phone takes the context from a backgrounded tab. The renderer already rebuilt itself on restore; only the app's flag stayed down.

nodes.title: gl/app.js: on webglcontextrestored the app is ok again and 3D resumes
Public /play/ is 3D in all eight chapters and both endings: 0 of ~198k frames drawn in 2D; context loss now returns to 3D
nodes.description: Nine playthroughs against the deployed site (emulated iPhone, touch, chapter 1 from its own card through chapter 8 both endings): every mode 3D, every line said, no tier step-downs. One transient HTTP 503 from Pages on one voice file (200 on retry). Lose/restore test in play (WEBGL_lose_context): 3D, 2D while lost, 3D again with the same draw counts. A 1280x800 window is 3D too. Fix deployed as mirror commit 29a1df9. Still 2D by design: ?gl=0, no WebGL2, and a 3D renderer that throws (retired for the session, logged). Seen and not fixed: in the wide layout a white light burst covers the top of the cutter-deck stage.
